definition_en: a motion picture, a thin strip of material for recording images, a thin layer, or to record something with a camera
core_image: 放映机的光穿过胶片，在墙上投出晃动的画面
scene: 我们昨晚看了一部关于海洋的电影。We watched a film about the ocean last night.
sceneCN: 这里 film 是「电影」（第 1 个义项）；句意：我们昨晚看了一部关于海洋的电影。

senses.title: Motion picture
senses.definition: a story or record shown in moving pictures
senses.definitionCN: 以活动画面讲述故事或记录事物的作品
senses.example: We watched a film about the ocean last night.
senses.exampleCN: 我们昨晚看了一部关于海洋的电影。
senses.why: This is the most common modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代最常见的义项。

senses.title: Photographic strip
senses.definition: a thin strip coated to record images
senses.definitionCN: 涂有感光层、用于记录影像的薄带
senses.example: The old camera still uses film.
senses.exampleCN: 这台旧相机仍使用胶片。
senses.why: Moving pictures were once recorded on film.
senses.whyCN: 活动画面曾被记录在胶片上。

senses.title: Thin layer
senses.definition: a very thin layer of material
senses.definitionCN: 一层极薄的材料
senses.example: A film of oil covered the water.
senses.exampleCN: 水面上覆着一层油膜。
senses.why: The oldest sense is a thin skin or layer.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是薄皮或薄层。

senses.title: To record
senses.definition: to record something with a camera
senses.definitionCN: 用摄影机记录某物
senses.example: They filmed the whole ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 他们拍摄了整场仪式。
senses.why: The material name becomes the action.
senses.whyCN: 材料名转化为动作。

intro.en: Film comes from Old English filmen, a thin skin or membrane.
intro.cn: film 源自古英语 filmen（薄皮、薄膜）。

items.en: Filmen meant a thin skin or membrane.
items.cn: filmen 意为薄皮或薄膜。

items.en: Film named a thin covering or haze.
items.cn: film 指薄薄的覆盖层或薄雾。

items.en: Photography gave film a light-sensitive strip.
items.cn: 摄影术使 film 指感光胶片。

items.en: Film came to mean a motion picture.
items.cn: film 进而指电影。

items.en: The verb means to record with a camera.
items.cn: 动词形式意为用摄影机拍摄。

note.en: Film is compared with similar-looking words and with words for movies and layers.
note.cn: 把 film 与形近词以及表示电影和薄层的词作比较。

entries.definition: the art or place of films
a thin layer over a surface

normalIntro.en: Film is a thin layer first, then a strip that carries pictures, then the pictures themselves.
normalIntro.cn: film 先是薄层，再是承载画面的胶片，最后指影片本身。

normal.en: A film can mean a movie.
Old cameras used film.
Soap leaves a film on the glass.
normal.cn: 肥皂在玻璃上留下一层薄膜。

normal.en: The verb means to record.
A filmmaker makes films.

abstract.en: A thin layer can hold a whole world of light.
abstract.cn: 薄薄一层也能承载整个光的世界。

abstract.en: Pictures in motion turn time into a story.
abstract.cn: 活动的画面把时间变成故事。

abstract.en: Recording is a way of refusing to forget.
abstract.cn: 记录是一种拒绝遗忘的方式。

examples.en: We watched a film about the ocean last night.
examples.cn: 我们昨晚看了一部关于海洋的电影。

examples.en: The old camera still uses film.
examples.cn: 这台旧相机仍使用胶片。

examples.en: A film of oil covered the water.
examples.cn: 水面上覆着一层油膜。

dict_mnemonic.text: film 源自古英语 filmen（薄皮），本义「薄层」，后指感光胶片，再指电影与拍摄。

root: 源自古英语 filmen（薄皮、薄膜），核心义「薄薄的一层」。

sensesIntro.en: Film means a movie, a photographic strip, a thin layer, or to record with a camera.
sensesIntro.cn: film 意为电影、胶片、薄膜或拍摄。

core.en: A thin layer that can carry images.
core.cn: 能承载影像的薄层。

branches.en: A story told in moving pictures.
branches.cn: 用活动画面讲述的故事。

branches.en: The strip and the recording share one word.
branches.cn: 胶片与拍摄共用一个词。

intro.en: Film belongs to the old Germanic family of thin coverings.
intro.cn: film 属于日耳曼语中表示薄覆盖层的古老词族。

latinIntro.en: Film has no Latin ancestor; Latin pellicula, a thin skin, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: film 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 pellicula（薄皮）只是语义对应词。

items.exampleCN: 这位电影制作人获奖了。

items.example: The scene has a filmic quality.
items.exampleCN: 这个场景有电影般的质感。

items.example: The records are stored on microfilm.
items.exampleCN: 这些记录存放在缩微胶片上。

definition_zh: 过滤器；滤光片；过滤；筛选
definition_en: a device that removes unwanted matter, a screen that changes light, to pass something through such a device, or to screen information
core_image: 咖啡一滴一滴穿过滤纸，落进下面的玻璃壶
scene: 咖啡慢慢通过滤纸滴进杯子里。The coffee dripped through the paper filter into the cup.
sceneCN: 这里 filter 是「过滤器」（第 1 个义项）；句意：咖啡慢慢通过滤纸滴进杯子里。

senses.title: Straining device
senses.definition: a device that removes unwanted matter from liquid or air
senses.definitionCN: 从液体或空气中除去杂质的装置
senses.example: The coffee dripped through the paper filter into the cup.
senses.exampleCN: 咖啡慢慢通过滤纸滴进杯子里。
senses.why: This is the basic device sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的装置义。

senses.title: Light screen
senses.definition: a screen that lets some light through and blocks the rest
senses.definitionCN: 让部分光通过而挡住其余光的镜片
senses.example: The photographer put a filter on the lens.
senses.exampleCN: 摄影师在镜头上装了滤光片。
senses.why: The device sense extends to light.
senses.whyCN: 装置义扩展到光线。

senses.title: To strain
senses.definition: to pass liquid or air through a filter
senses.definitionCN: 使液体或空气通过过滤器
senses.example: They filter the water before drinking it.
senses.exampleCN: 他们喝水前先过滤。
senses.why: The noun turns into the action.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为动作。

senses.title: To screen
senses.definition: to remove unwanted information or people
senses.definitionCN: 剔除不需要的信息或人员
senses.example: The software filters spam from email.
senses.exampleCN: 这款软件从邮件中筛除垃圾信息。
senses.why: Filtering applies to data as well as liquid.
senses.whyCN: 过滤也适用于数据，而不只是液体。

intro.en: Filter comes from Medieval Latin filtrum, felt, used as a strainer, through Old French filtre.
intro.cn: filter 出自中世纪拉丁语 filtrum（毛毡），因毛毡可用作滤材，经古法语 filtre 而来。

items.en: Filtrum meant felt used for straining.
items.cn: filtrum 指用于过滤的毛毡。

items.en: Filtre meant a strainer.
items.cn: filtre 意为过滤器。

items.en: Filter named a cloth or device for straining.
items.cn: 英语 filter 指过滤用布或装置。

items.en: Filters also treat air and engine fuel.
items.cn: 过滤器也用于处理空气与发动机燃料。

items.en: The verb extends to screening information.
items.cn: 动词形式扩展到筛选信息。

note.en: Filter is compared with similar-looking words and with words for straining and screening.
note.cn: 把 filter 与形近词以及表示过滤和筛选的词作比较。

entries.definition: something used to fill a space
liquid that has passed a filter
a device for separating solids from liquid
a mesh for separating fine matter

normalIntro.en: A filter lets what is wanted through and holds back the rest.
normalIntro.cn: 过滤器让需要的东西通过，把其余部分留下。

normal.en: A coffee filter holds the grounds.
An air filter keeps dust out.
Filter out means to remove.
The noun and verb look the same.
A filtrate is what passes through.
normal.cn: filtrate 是透过滤器的液体。

abstract.en: To filter is to choose what may pass.
abstract.cn: 过滤就是选择什么可以通过。

abstract.en: Attention is a filter for a noisy world.
abstract.cn: 注意力是应对喧闹世界的过滤器。

abstract.en: What is held back can be as important as what gets through.
abstract.cn: 被挡住的东西可以和通过的一样重要。

examples.en: The coffee dripped through the paper filter into the cup.
examples.cn: 咖啡慢慢通过滤纸滴进杯子里。

examples.en: They filter the water before drinking it.
examples.cn: 他们喝水前先过滤。

examples.en: The software filters spam from email.
examples.cn: 这款软件从邮件中筛除垃圾信息。

dict_mnemonic.text: filter 出自中世纪拉丁语 filtrum（毛毡），因毛毡可作滤材，本义「滤布」，后指过滤器、滤光片与筛选。

root: 源自中世纪拉丁语 filtrum（毛毡），核心义「让一部分通过、拦住其余」。

sensesIntro.en: Filter means a straining device, a light screen, to strain, or to screen information.
sensesIntro.cn: filter 意为过滤器、滤光片、过滤或筛选。

core.en: A barrier that selects what passes.
core.cn: 挑选何物可通过的屏障。

branches.en: A device for liquid or air.
branches.cn: 用于液体或空气的装置。

branches.en: Liquid and information obey the same idea.
branches.cn: 液体与信息遵循同一观念。

intro.en: Filter belongs to the Medieval Latin filtrum family of straining.
intro.cn: filter 属于中世纪拉丁语 filtrum（毛毡）词族，关联过滤。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin filtrum is the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 filtrum 是历史词根。

items.exampleCN: 这家工厂使用三个过滤器。

items.example: Collect the filtrate in a jar.
The filterless pipe lets ash through.
items.exampleCN: 没有滤嘴的烟斗会漏进烟灰。

definition_zh: 最后的；最终的；决赛；期末考试
definition_en: coming at the end, deciding a matter, the last game in a competition, or the last examination
core_image: 赛场上最后一声哨响，记分牌定格
scene: 这是本季的最后一集。This is the final episode of the season.
sceneCN: 这里 final 是「最后的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这是本季的最后一集。

senses.title: Last in order
senses.definition: coming at the end of a series
senses.definitionCN: 出现在一系列事物的末尾
senses.example: This is the final episode of the season.
senses.exampleCN: 这是本季的最后一集。
senses.why: This is the basic order sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的次序义。

senses.title: Decisive
senses.definition: settling a matter and not to be changed
senses.definitionCN: 决定事情且不再更改
senses.example: The judge's decision is final.
senses.exampleCN: 法官的判决是最终的。
senses.why: What comes last also settles the matter.
senses.whyCN: 最后出现的东西也了结事情。

senses.title: Championship game
senses.definition: the last game in a competition
senses.definitionCN: 比赛中的最后一场
senses.example: They reached the final.
senses.exampleCN: 他们进入了决赛。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a noun for the last match.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转为指最后一场比赛的名词。

senses.title: Last examination
senses.definition: the last examination of a course
senses.definitionCN: 一门课程的最后一次考试
senses.example: She is studying for her finals.
senses.exampleCN: 她正在为期末考试复习。
senses.why: The last test is called the final.
senses.whyCN: 最后一次考试被称为期末考。

intro.en: Final comes from Latin finalis, of an end, from finis, end or boundary.
intro.cn: final 出自拉丁语 finalis（末尾的），源于 finis（终点、界限）。

items.en: Finis meant end or boundary.
items.cn: finis 意为终点或界限。

items.en: Finalis meant relating to the end.
items.cn: finalis 意为与末尾有关的。

items.en: Old French final kept the end sense.
items.cn: 古法语 final 保留了末尾义。

items.en: English final named the last in order.
items.cn: 英语 final 指次序上的最后。

items.en: It also names the last match and exam.
items.cn: 它也指最后一场比赛与考试。

note.en: Final is compared with similar-looking words and with words for last and decisive.
note.cn: 把 final 与形近词以及表示最后与决定性的词作比较。

entries.definition: the last part of a show

normalIntro.en: Final marks the end, whether of a series, a decision, a match, or a course.
normalIntro.cn: final 标记终点，无论系列、决定、比赛还是课程。

normal.en: Final means last in order.
normal.cn: final 意为次序上的最后。

normal.en: A final decision cannot be changed easily.
The final is the last game.
Finals are end-of-term exams.
Finalize means to make final.

abstract.en: Every end gives shape to what came before.
abstract.cn: 每个终点都赋予此前经历以形状。

abstract.en: A last word can close a long argument.
abstract.cn: 最后一句话能结束漫长的争论。

abstract.en: The final step is often the one that counts.
abstract.cn: 最后一步往往才是关键。

examples.en: This is the final episode of the season.
examples.cn: 这是本季的最后一集。

examples.en: The judge's decision is final.
examples.cn: 法官的判决是最终的。

examples.en: They reached the final.
examples.cn: 他们进入了决赛。

dict_mnemonic.text: final 出自拉丁语 finis（终点、界限），本义「位于末尾的」，后指决定性的、决赛与期末考试。

root: 源自拉丁语 finis（终点），核心义「位于末尾、了结事情」。

sensesIntro.en: Final means last, decisive, the championship game, or the last examination.
sensesIntro.cn: final 意为最后的、最终的、决赛或期末考试。

core.en: The point where something ends.
core.cn: 事物结束的那一点。

branches.en: The last item in a series.
A decision that closes a matter.
The last match of a competition.
The last exam of a course.
Being last and being decisive meet at the end.
branches.cn: 最后与决定性在终点相遇。

intro.en: Final belongs to the Latin finis family of ends and limits.
intro.cn: final 属于拉丁语 finis（终点、界限）词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin finis and finalis are the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 finis 与 finalis 是历史词根。

items.example: We will finalize the plan today.
She is a finalist this year.

definition_en: after a long time, as the last point, or in a way that settles a matter
core_image: 钟表的指针走过很久，门终于被推开
scene: 等了两个小时，公交车终于来了。After two hours, the bus finally arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 finally 是「终于」（第 1 个义项）；句意：等了两个小时，公交车终于来了。

senses.title: At last
senses.definition: after a long wait or effort
senses.definitionCN: 经过漫长的等待或努力之后
senses.example: After two hours, the bus finally arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 等了两个小时，公交车终于来了。
senses.why: This is the most common sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最常见的义项。

senses.title: As the last point
senses.definition: as the last item in a list or argument
senses.definitionCN: 作为列表或论述中的最后一项
senses.example: Finally, I want to thank my teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 最后，我想感谢我的老师。
senses.why: The order sense comes from final.
senses.whyCN: 次序义来自 final。

senses.title: Decisively
senses.definition: in a way that settles a matter
senses.definitionCN: 以了结事情的方式
senses.example: The matter was finally settled.
senses.exampleCN: 这件事最终得到解决。
senses.why: A final act closes what was open.
senses.whyCN: 最终的行动了结未决之事。

intro.cn: finally 由 final 加 -ly 构成，源自拉丁语 finis（终点）。

items.en: Final entered English as an adjective.
items.cn: final 作为形容词进入英语。

items.en: The adverb added -ly for manner and order.
items.cn: 副词加 -ly，表示方式与次序。

items.en: Finally also marks a long-awaited result.
items.cn: finally 也标记久等之后的结果。

note.en: Finally is compared with similar-looking words and with words for time and order.

normalIntro.en: Finally marks the end of a wait, a list, or an open question.

abstract.en: Some things arrive only after we stop counting.

examples.en: After two hours, the bus finally arrived.

branches.en: The end of a long wait.

definition_zh: 金融；财政；资金；为……提供资金

scene: 这家公司需要资金来扩大生产。The company needs finance to expand production.

senses.title: Money management
senses.definition: the management of money and investment
senses.definitionCN: 对货币与投资的管理
senses.example: She works in finance.
senses.exampleCN: 她从事金融工作。
senses.why: This is the broad field sense.

senses.title: Public revenue

senses.definitionCN: 政府的收入与支出
senses.example: Public finance pays for roads and schools.
senses.exampleCN: 公共财政支付道路与学校。
senses.why: The field sense narrows to government.

senses.title: Funds

senses.definitionCN: 项目所需的钱

senses.exampleCN: 这家公司需要资金来扩大生产。
senses.why: Money for a purpose is finance.
senses.whyCN: 为某个目的准备的钱就是资金。

senses.title: To fund
senses.definition: to provide money for something
senses.definitionCN: 为某事提供资金
senses.example: The city financed the new bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 市政府为新桥提供资金。
senses.why: The noun becomes the act of providing money.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为提供资金的动作。

items.en: Finis meant end or boundary.
items.cn: finis 意为终点或界限。

items.en: Finer meant to settle a debt.
items.cn: finer 意为了结债务。

items.en: Finance named the settling of money matters.
items.cn: finance 指钱财事务的了结。

items.en: Finance named the management of money.
items.cn: finance 指对金钱的管理。

note.en: Finance is compared with similar-looking words and with words for money matters.

coins and notes used to pay

normalIntro.en: Finance is money managed, money raised, and money provided.
normalIntro.cn: finance 是被管理的钱、被筹集的资金与被提供的款项。

normal.en: Finance began with settling debts.
normal.cn: finance 最初与了结债务有关。

normal.en: Public finance belongs to the state.
A project needs finance to start.
normal.cn: 项目需要资金才能启动。

normal.en: To finance is to pay for something.
normal.cn: to finance 意为为某事出钱。

normal.en: The adjective is financial.

abstract.en: Money is stored effort, moved from hand to hand.
abstract.cn: 钱是储存起来的劳动，从一只手流到另一只手。

abstract.en: A budget is a promise about the future.
abstract.cn: 预算是一份关于未来的承诺。

abstract.en: What a society funds shows what it values.
abstract.cn: 一个社会资助什么，就显示它重视什么。

examples.en: The company needs finance to expand production.
examples.cn: 这家公司需要资金来扩大生产。

examples.en: She works in finance.
examples.cn: 她从事金融工作。

examples.en: The city financed the new bridge.
examples.cn: 市政府为新桥提供资金。

dict_mnemonic.text: finance 出自中古法语 finance（清偿债务），源于 finer（了结），本义「结清钱款」，后指金融、财政、资金与提供资金。

root: 源自拉丁语 finis（终点）经法语 finer（了结），核心义「了结钱款、管理钱财」。

sensesIntro.en: Finance means money management, public revenue, project funds, or to provide money.
sensesIntro.cn: finance 意为金融、财政、资金或提供资金。

core.en: Money brought under control and put to use.
core.cn: 被管理并投入使用的金钱。

branches.cn: 为某个目的筹集的资金。

branches.en: The act of paying for something.
The field and the funds share one name.
branches.cn: 领域与资金共用一个名称。

intro.en: Finance belongs to the Latin finis family of settling and ending.
intro.cn: finance 属于拉丁语 finis（终点）词族，关联了结与结算。

latinIntro.en: Latin finis and French finer are the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 finis 与法语 finer 是历史词根。

items.exampleCN: 一家银行为这笔交易提供资金。

items.example: The financial year ends in March.

items.exampleCN: 这位金融家资助了这个项目。

definition_en: relating to money, banking, or the management of funds
core_image: 银行大厅的屏幕上，一排排数字不停地跳动
scene: 这家公司正陷入财务困境。The company is in financial trouble.
sceneCN: 这里 financial 是「财务的」（第 3 个义项）；句意：这家公司正陷入财务困境。

senses.title: Banking and investment
senses.definition: relating to banks, investments, and money markets
senses.definitionCN: 与银行、投资和货币市场有关的
senses.example: She works in the financial sector.
senses.exampleCN: 她在金融行业工作。
senses.why: This sense points to banks and investment.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项指向银行与投资领域。

senses.title: Public revenue
senses.definition: relating to the money of a government
senses.definitionCN: 与政府收支有关的
senses.example: The city faces a financial shortfall.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市面临财政短缺。
senses.why: Governments also manage money.
senses.whyCN: 政府同样要管理资金。

senses.title: Company accounts
senses.definition: relating to the money and accounts of a business
senses.definitionCN: 与企业的资金和账目有关的
senses.example: The company is in financial trouble.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司正陷入财务困境。
senses.why: A business keeps its own accounts.
senses.whyCN: 企业有自己的账目要管。

intro.en: Financial goes back to Latin finis, an end, through French finance, a payment that settles a debt.
intro.cn: financial 上溯至拉丁语 finis（结束），经法语 finance（结清债务的付款）演变而来。

items.en: Finis meant an end or a boundary.
items.cn: finis 意为终点或边界。

items.en: Finare meant to settle a debt.
items.cn: finare 意为结清债务。

items.en: Finance named a payment or revenue.
items.cn: finance 指付款或收入。

items.en: Finance came to mean money management.
items.cn: finance 进而指资金管理。

items.en: The adjective financial described money matters.
items.cn: 形容词 financial 用来描述资金事务。

note.en: Financial is compared with similar-looking words and with words about money.
note.cn: 把 financial 与形近词以及表示金钱的词作比较。

entries.definition: a person who deals in money

normalIntro.en: Financial is the adjective of finance, so it describes anything that involves money.
normalIntro.cn: financial 是 finance 的形容词，用来描述一切与金钱有关的事物。

normal.en: A financial crisis shakes the banks.
Financial aid helps students pay fees.
normal.cn: 经济援助帮学生支付学费。

normal.en: A financial adviser plans your money.
normal.cn: 理财顾问为你的钱做规划。

normal.en: The company reports financial results each year.
normal.cn: 公司每年公布财务业绩。

normal.en: Financial trouble means the money is short.
normal.cn: 财务困境意味着资金短缺。

abstract.en: Money is a promise that people agree to trust.
abstract.cn: 金钱是人们约定去信任的一种承诺。

abstract.en: A financial system turns trust into numbers.
abstract.cn: 金融体系把信任变成了数字。

abstract.en: Every account is a story of choices made.
abstract.cn: 每一本账目都是选择的故事。

examples.en: The company is in financial trouble.
examples.cn: 这家公司正陷入财务困境。

examples.en: She works in the financial sector.
examples.cn: 她在金融行业工作。

examples.en: They offered financial support to the family.
examples.cn: 他们向这家人提供了资金支持。

dict_mnemonic.text: financial 来自 finance（金融），加形容词后缀 -ial，表示「与资金有关的」。

root: 源自拉丁语 finis（结束），经法语 finance（结算、收入）演变为「财政、金融」。

sensesIntro.en: Financial describes matters of banking, public revenue, or company accounts.
sensesIntro.cn: financial 描述银行、政府收支或企业账目方面的事务。

core.en: Everything that belongs to money and its management.
core.cn: 一切属于金钱及其管理的事物。

branches.en: Both deal with large sums of money.
Public and private books share the word.
branches.cn: 公共与私人账目共用一词。

intro.en: Financial is built from the noun finance plus the adjective suffix -ial.
intro.cn: financial 由名词 finance 加形容词后缀 -ial 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root finis, an end, also gave finish and final.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 finis（结束）也孕育了 finish 与 final。

items.exampleCN: 这个项目在财务上是稳健的。

items.example: The bridge was financed by the city.

items.exampleCN: 这位金融家资助了铁路。

latinEntries.example: Finis marks the end of a debt.
Finare meant to end a debt by paying.
latinEntries.exampleCN: finare 意为付款了结债务。

definition_en: to discover something by searching, to come upon something, to consider something to be a certain way, or to make a legal decision
core_image: 手伸进沙发缝里，摸到那串丢失的钥匙
scene: 她在沙发后面找到了丢失的钥匙。She found the lost keys behind the sofa.
sceneCN: 这里 find 是「找到」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她在沙发后面找到了丢失的钥匙。

senses.title: To locate by searching
senses.definition: to discover something you have been looking for
senses.definitionCN: 找到一直在寻找的东西
senses.example: She found the lost keys behind the sofa.
senses.exampleCN: 她在沙发后面找到了丢失的钥匙。
senses.why: This is the everyday sense of searching.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常生活中搜寻的义项。

senses.title: To come upon
senses.definition: to discover something without looking for it
senses.definitionCN: 无意中遇到或发现某物
senses.example: We found a small café near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在车站附近发现了一家小咖啡馆。
senses.why: Some things are found by chance.
senses.whyCN: 有些东西是偶然发现的。

senses.title: To consider
senses.definition: to feel or think that something is a certain way
senses.definitionCN: 觉得或认为某事是某种样子
senses.example: I find this book very useful.
senses.exampleCN: 我觉得这本书很有用。
senses.why: Experience shapes our judgment.
senses.whyCN: 经历会影响我们的判断。

senses.title: To decide a case
senses.definition: to make a legal decision about a case
senses.definitionCN: 对案件作出法律裁定
senses.example: The jury found him innocent.
senses.exampleCN: 陪审团裁定他无罪。
senses.why: A court also reaches a finding.
senses.whyCN: 法庭也会给出裁断。

intro.en: Find comes from Old English findan, to come upon, and has kept that core meaning for over a thousand years.
intro.cn: find 源自古英语 findan（遇到、发现），一千多年来一直保留着这个核心含义。

items.en: Findan meant to come upon something.
items.cn: findan 意为遇到某物。

items.en: The verb also covered opinion and judgment.
items.cn: 这个动词也包含看法与判断。

items.en: Found became the past tense.
items.cn: found 成为过去式。

items.en: Find out extended the idea of discovery.
items.cn: find out 扩展了发现的含义。

items.en: Legal use named the verdict of a court.
items.cn: 法律用法指法庭的裁断。

note.en: Find is compared with similar-looking words and with words for discovery.
note.cn: 把 find 与形近词以及表示发现的词作比较。

entries.definition: a sum of money set aside
to learn or notice for the first time
to find the exact place of

normalIntro.en: Find is the plain verb for coming upon something, whether by search or by chance.
normalIntro.cn: find 是表示遇到某物的基本动词，无论靠寻找还是靠偶然。

normal.en: You find what you look for.
normal.cn: 你寻找的东西会被你找到。

normal.en: We found a café by chance.
normal.cn: 我们偶然发现了一家咖啡馆。

normal.en: Find out means to learn a fact.
normal.cn: find out 意为查明一个事实。

normal.en: A jury can find a person innocent.
normal.cn: 陪审团可以裁定一个人无罪。

normal.en: The past tense of find is found.

abstract.en: To find is to close the distance between wanting and having.
abstract.cn: 找到，就是缩短渴望与拥有之间的距离。

abstract.en: Some discoveries arrive without a search.
abstract.cn: 有些发现并不需要寻找。

abstract.en: What we find often changes what we were looking for.
abstract.cn: 我们找到的东西，常常改变我们原本寻找的东西。

examples.en: She found the lost keys behind the sofa.
examples.cn: 她在沙发后面找到了丢失的钥匙。

examples.en: We found a small café near the station.
examples.cn: 我们在车站附近发现了一家小咖啡馆。

examples.en: I find this book very useful.
examples.cn: 我觉得这本书很有用。

dict_mnemonic.text: find 源自古英语 findan（遇到），不规则变化为 find、found、found。

root: 源自古英语 findan（遇到、发现），核心义「遇见并得到」。

sensesIntro.en: Find means to locate, to come upon, to consider, or to give a legal decision.
sensesIntro.cn: find 意为找到、发现、认为或作出裁决。

core.en: To come upon something or someone.
core.cn: 遇到某物或某人。

branches.en: Chance and judgment both begin with meeting.
branches.cn: 偶然与判断都始于遇见。

intro.en: Find is a native Germanic verb with a strong and irregular past tense.
intro.cn: find 是日耳曼语本族动词，过去式强变化且不规则。

latinIntro.en: Find has no Latin ancestor; Latin invenire, to come upon, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: find 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 invenire（遇到）只是语义对应词。

items.example: She finds new ideas every day.
items.exampleCN: 她每天都能发现新想法。

items.meaningCN: 找到（过去式与过去分词）

items.exampleCN: 找到答案花了几个小时。

items.example: The findings were published last week.

items.exampleCN: 他带着新获得的自信说话。

items.example: The file is findable by name.
items.exampleCN: 这个文件可以按名称找到。

definition_zh: 好的；精美的；晴朗的；细小的；罚款
definition_en: of high quality, delicate or carefully made, bright and clear, very small, or a sum of money paid as a penalty
core_image: 雨后天空干净透亮，远山的轮廓都看得很清楚
scene: 今天天气很好，正适合散步。The weather is fine today, perfect for a walk.
sceneCN: 这里 fine 是「晴朗的」（第 3 个义项）；句意：今天天气很好，正适合散步。

senses.title: Of high quality
senses.definition: very good or of high quality
senses.definitionCN: 很好或质量很高的
senses.example: She is a fine musician.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一位出色的音乐家。
senses.why: The core sense praises quality.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是对品质的称赞。

senses.title: Delicately made
senses.definition: delicate, thin, or carefully made
senses.definitionCN: 精致、纤细或做工讲究的
senses.example: The dress has fine lace.
senses.exampleCN: 这条裙子有精美的蕾丝。
senses.why: Fine work is work done with care.
senses.whyCN: 精细的活计是用心做出来的。

senses.title: Bright and clear
senses.definition: sunny and clear, without rain
senses.definitionCN: 阳光充足、晴朗无雨的
senses.example: The weather is fine today, perfect for a walk.
senses.exampleCN: 今天天气很好，正适合散步。
senses.why: Clear weather is also called fine.
senses.whyCN: 晴朗的天气也称作 fine。

senses.title: Very small
senses.definition: very thin or made of tiny particles
senses.definitionCN: 极细的或由微小颗粒组成的
senses.example: Fine dust covered the shelf.
senses.exampleCN: 细小的灰尘落满了架子。
senses.why: Thin strands and grains are fine.
senses.whyCN: 细丝与细颗粒都可用 fine。

senses.title: Money penalty
senses.definition: a sum of money paid as a punishment
senses.definitionCN: 作为惩罚支付的一笔钱
senses.example: He had to pay a parking fine.
senses.exampleCN: 他不得不缴纳违章停车罚款。
senses.why: The noun names the payment that ends a case.
senses.whyCN: 名词指了结案件的这笔付款。

intro.en: Fine comes from Latin finis, an end, and first meant finished or perfected.
intro.cn: fine 源自拉丁语 finis（结束），最初意为「完成的、完善的」。

items.en: Finis meant an end or a limit.
items.cn: finis 意为终点或界限。

items.en: Fin meant finished or perfected.
items.cn: fin 意为完成的或完善的。

items.en: Fine came to mean of high quality.
items.cn: fine 逐渐指品质优良。

items.en: The word extended to clear weather and thin particles.
items.cn: 这个词又扩展到晴朗天气与细小颗粒。

items.en: The noun named a money penalty.
items.cn: 名词形式指金钱处罚。

note.en: Fine is compared with similar-looking words and with words for quality and penalties.
note.cn: 把 fine 与形近词以及表示品质和处罚的词作比较。

entries.definition: a punishment for breaking a rule

normalIntro.en: Fine stretches from perfect quality to thin particles and even to a sum of money.
normalIntro.cn: fine 从完美的品质一路延伸到细小颗粒，甚至一笔罚金。

normal.en: Fine weather is clear and sunny.
normal.cn: fine weather 指晴朗的天气。

normal.en: Fine lace is delicate and beautiful.
normal.cn: 精细的蕾丝既纤巧又美丽。

normal.en: Fine dust floats in the air.
normal.cn: 细小的灰尘飘浮在空气中。

normal.en: A fine is money paid for a rule broken.
normal.cn: 罚款是因违规而支付的钱。

normal.en: The finest work takes the most care.
normal.cn: 最精细的作品需要最用心。

abstract.en: To finish something is to make it fine.
abstract.cn: 把一件事做完，就是把它做精。

abstract.en: What is fine can be either perfect or merely thin.
abstract.cn: fine 既可以是完美，也可以只是纤细。

abstract.en: A line between good and bad is often a fine one.
abstract.cn: 好坏之间的界线往往只有一线之差。

examples.en: The weather is fine today, perfect for a walk.
examples.cn: 今天天气很好，正适合散步。

examples.en: She is a fine musician.
examples.cn: 她是一位出色的音乐家。

examples.en: Fine dust covered the shelf.
examples.cn: 细小的灰尘落满了架子。

dict_mnemonic.text: fine 源自拉丁语 finis（结束），本义「完成的、完善的」，后引申出晴朗、纤细与罚款。

root: 源自拉丁语 finis（结束、界限），核心义「到了尽头的圆满」。

sensesIntro.en: Fine means excellent, delicate, clear, very small, or a money penalty.
sensesIntro.cn: fine 意为优良的、精美的、晴朗的、细小的或罚款。

core.en: Something brought to its finished, perfect state.
core.cn: 被带到完成、圆满状态的事物。

branches.cn: 用心之作造就精致之物。
晴朗天空让人感到完美。

branches.en: Tiny grains are the finest form.
branches.cn: 微小颗粒是最细的形态。

branches.en: A payment ends a legal case.
branches.cn: 一笔付款了结一桩案件。

intro.en: Fine is a short Latin-derived word that grows many relatives through prefixes and suffixes.
intro.cn: fine 源自拉丁语，词形简短，通过前缀和后缀衍生出许多同族词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root finis, an end, links fine with finish, final, and finance.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 finis（结束）把 fine 与 finish、final、finance 联系起来。

items.example: This thread is finer than that one.
The fineness of the powder matters.
The oil refinery runs day and night.

latinEntries.example: Finis gave fine its sense of completion.
latinEntries.exampleCN: finis 赋予 fine「完成」的含义。

latinEntries.example: Finire led to the English word finish.
latinEntries.exampleCN: finire 演变为英语单词 finish。

definition_en: into very small pieces, with great delicacy, or in a very good way
core_image: 刀刃落下，洋葱被切成几乎透明的薄片
scene: 厨师把洋葱切得很细。The chef chopped the onions finely.
sceneCN: 这里 finely 是「细小地」（第 2 个义项）；句意：厨师把洋葱切得很细。

senses.title: With delicate skill
senses.definition: with delicate care or detailed workmanship
senses.definitionCN: 以细致的用心或工艺完成的
senses.example: The wood was finely carved.
senses.exampleCN: 这块木头雕刻得很精细。
senses.why: This sense stresses careful craft.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项强调用心的手艺。

senses.title: Into tiny pieces
senses.definition: cut or ground into very small pieces
senses.definitionCN: 被切碎或磨成很小的颗粒
senses.example: The chef chopped the onions finely.
senses.exampleCN: 厨师把洋葱切得很细。
senses.why: Thin pieces are called fine.
senses.whyCN: 细碎的小块被称为 fine。

senses.title: Very well
senses.definition: in a very good or excellent way
senses.definitionCN: 以很好、很出色的方式
senses.example: She performed finely under pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 她在压力下表现得很好。
senses.why: Fine quality extends to how an action is done.
senses.whyCN: 优良的品质也延伸到做事的程度上。

intro.en: Finely is fine plus the adverb suffix -ly, so it inherits the whole history of fine.
intro.cn: finely 由 fine 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，因此继承了 fine 的全部历史。

items.en: Finis meant an end or limit.
items.cn: finis 意为终点或界限。

items.en: Fin meant finished or perfected.
items.cn: fin 意为完成的或完善的。

items.en: Fine meant of high quality.
items.cn: fine 意为品质优良的。

items.en: The adverb finely described delicate action.
items.cn: 副词 finely 描述细致的动作。

items.en: Finely also came to mean in tiny pieces.
items.cn: finely 又引申为「细碎地」。

note.en: Finely is compared with similar-looking words and with adverbs of precision.
note.cn: 把 finely 与形近词以及表示精确的副词作比较。

entries.definition: in a gentle and careful way

normalIntro.en: Finely tells how something is done with care or cut into tiny pieces.
normalIntro.cn: finely 说明动作是精细完成的，或被切成细小的部分。

normal.en: Chop the herbs finely.
The fabric is finely woven.
A finely tuned engine runs smoothly.
normal.cn: 调校精良的引擎运转顺畅。

normal.en: The balance is finely set.
Finely ground coffee smells strong.
normal.cn: 磨得很细的咖啡香气浓烈。

abstract.en: Precision is patience made visible.
abstract.cn: 精确是耐心变得可见的样子。

abstract.en: Small cuts can shape a larger whole.
abstract.cn: 细小的刀工也能塑造更大的整体。

abstract.en: To do a thing finely is to respect the material.
abstract.cn: 把事情做精细，就是尊重材料本身。

examples.en: The chef chopped the onions finely.
examples.cn: 厨师把洋葱切得很细。

examples.en: The wood was finely carved.
examples.cn: 这块木头雕刻得很精细。

examples.en: The instrument was finely tuned.
examples.cn: 这件乐器被调校得很精细。

dict_mnemonic.text: finely 由 fine（精细的）加副词后缀 -ly 构成，表示「精细地、细碎地」。

root: 由 fine（源自拉丁语 finis，完成、完善）加 -ly 构成。

sensesIntro.en: Finely means with delicate skill, in tiny pieces, or very well.
sensesIntro.cn: finely 意为精细地、细碎地或很好地。

core.en: Doing something in a fine, careful manner.
core.cn: 以精细、用心的方式做某事。

branches.cn: 以细致用心完成的工艺。
被切成细碎小块的物料。

branches.en: Skill and quality meet in the adverb.
branches.cn: 技艺与品质在这个副词中相遇。

branches.en: Fine pieces and fine performance share one form.
branches.cn: 细碎与出色共用一个形式。

intro.en: Finely is formed by adding the adverb suffix -ly to the adjective fine.
intro.cn: finely 由形容词 fine 加副词后缀 -ly 构成。

latinIntro.en: The base fine goes back to Latin finis, an end.

items.example: Fine threads are hard to see.
Only the finest flour is used.
The fineness of the sand surprised us.

items.example: They refine metal in this plant.

这个设计还需要进一步改进。

latinEntries.example: Finis lies behind fine and finely.
latinEntries.exampleCN: finis 是 fine 与 finely 的词源根基。

definition_zh: 手指；指状物；用手指触碰
definition_en: one of the long parts of the hand, a part shaped like a finger, or to touch something with the fingers
core_image: 指尖落在琴键上，轻轻按下一个音
scene: 他用手指点了点地图上的位置。He pointed a finger at the spot on the map.
sceneCN: 这里 finger 是「手指」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他用手指点了点地图上的位置。

senses.title: Part of the hand
senses.definition: one of the long thin parts at the end of the hand
senses.definitionCN: 手末端细长的部位之一
senses.example: He pointed a finger at the spot on the map.
senses.exampleCN: 他用手指点了点地图上的位置。
senses.why: This is the basic body-part sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的身体部位义项。

senses.title: Finger-shaped part
senses.definition: something long and narrow that looks like a finger
senses.definitionCN: 细长、形似手指的东西
senses.example: A finger of light came through the curtain.
senses.exampleCN: 一道指状的光从窗帘缝里透进来。
senses.why: Shape names many objects by analogy.
senses.whyCN: 人们常用形状来类比命名物体。

senses.title: To touch with fingers
senses.definition: to touch or handle something with the fingers
senses.definitionCN: 用手指触摸或摆弄某物
senses.example: He fingered the coin in his pocket.
senses.exampleCN: 他在口袋里用手指摩挲那枚硬币。
senses.why: The body part becomes a verb of touch.
senses.whyCN: 身体部位转化为触摸的动作。

intro.en: Finger is an old Germanic word, recorded in Old English as finger, with the same meaning it has today.
intro.cn: finger 是古老的日耳曼词，古英语中写作 finger，含义与今天相同。

items.en: Fingraz named a finger of the hand.
items.cn: fingraz 指手上的手指。

items.en: Finger kept the same meaning.
items.cn: finger 保留了相同的含义。

items.en: Fingers named finger-shaped parts.
items.cn: fingers 开始指形似手指的部件。

items.en: The verb meant to touch with the fingers.
items.cn: 动词形式意为用手指触碰。

items.en: Compounds such as fingertip appeared.
items.cn: fingertip 等复合词出现。

note.en: Finger is compared with similar-looking words and with words for hand parts.
note.cn: 把 finger 与形近词以及表示手部部位的词作比较。

entries.definition: the short thick digit of the hand

normalIntro.en: Finger names the long parts of the hand and also anything shaped like one.
normalIntro.cn: finger 指手上细长的部位，也指任何形似手指的东西。

normal.en: The index finger points the way.
She crossed her fingers for luck.
A finger of light entered the room.
normal.cn: 一道指状的光射进房间。

normal.en: Finger food is eaten by hand.
Fingertip is the end of a finger.

abstract.en: A finger can point, hold, feel, and speak.
abstract.cn: 一根手指能指、能握、能感觉，也能表达。

abstract.en: The smallest part of the hand can do the finest work.
abstract.cn: 手上最小的部分，能完成最精细的工作。

abstract.en: To point a finger is also to place blame.
abstract.cn: 伸出手指，有时也是把责任指向别人。

examples.en: He pointed a finger at the spot on the map.
examples.cn: 他用手指点了点地图上的位置。

examples.en: A finger of light came through the curtain.
examples.cn: 一道指状的光从窗帘缝里透进来。

examples.en: He fingered the coin in his pocket.
examples.cn: 他在口袋里用手指摩挲那枚硬币。

dict_mnemonic.text: finger 是日耳曼语本族词，核心义「手指」，也可指形似手指的细长物。

root: 源自古英语 finger（手指），与德语 Finger 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Finger means a part of the hand, a finger-shaped thing, or to touch with the fingers.
sensesIntro.cn: finger 意为手指、指状物或用手指触碰。

core.en: A long, narrow part of the hand used to touch and point.
core.cn: 手上用于触碰和指示的细长部位。

branches.en: The part and its action share a form.
branches.cn: 部位与动作共用一个形式。

branches.en: Shape links the hand to the world.
branches.cn: 形状把手指与世界联系起来。

intro.en: Finger is a native Germanic word that forms many compounds.
intro.cn: finger 是日耳曼语本族词，能构成许多复合词。

latinIntro.en: Finger has no Latin ancestor; Latin digitus, a finger, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: finger 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 digitus（手指）只是语义对应词。

items.exampleCN: 她用手指摸了摸柔软的布。

items.example: The fingering of the strings was light.
The answer is at your fingertips.

items.exampleCN: 这种植物有指状的叶子。

definition_zh: 完成；结束；终点；表面处理
definition_en: to complete something, to come to an end, the end of something, or a surface treatment
core_image: 笔尖在最后一题上停住，试卷被轻轻合上
scene: 她答完最后一题，放下了笔。She finished the last question and put down her pen.
sceneCN: 这里 finish 是「完成」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她答完最后一题，放下了笔。

senses.title: To complete
senses.definition: to bring a task or activity to its end
senses.definitionCN: 把任务或活动做到结尾
senses.example: She finished the last question and put down her pen.
senses.exampleCN: 她答完最后一题，放下了笔。
senses.why: This is the most common everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最常见的日常义项。

senses.title: To come to an end
senses.definition: to stop or end, especially at a planned time
senses.definitionCN: 停止或结束，尤指在预定时间结束
senses.example: The meeting finished at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 会议在中午结束。
senses.why: Events as well as tasks can finish.
senses.whyCN: 不只是任务，事件也会结束。

senses.title: The end of a race
senses.definition: the last part or end of something, such as a race
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的最后部分或终点，如比赛的终点
senses.example: The race had a close finish.
senses.exampleCN: 这场比赛的最后阶段竞争激烈。
senses.why: The noun names the ending point.
senses.whyCN: 名词形式指结束的那个点。

senses.title: Surface treatment
senses.definition: the way a surface is treated or coated
senses.definitionCN: 表层的处理方式或涂层
senses.example: The table has a smooth finish.
senses.exampleCN: 这张桌子表面很光滑。
senses.why: A finished surface is the last stage of making.
senses.whyCN: 表面处理是制作过程的最后一步。

intro.en: Finish comes from Latin finis, an end, through Old French finir, to bring to an end.
intro.cn: finish 源自拉丁语 finis（结束），经古法语 finir（使结束）传入英语。

items.en: Finis meant an end or boundary.
items.cn: finis 意为终点或边界。

items.en: Finir meant to bring to an end.
items.cn: finir 意为使某事结束。

items.en: Finishen meant to complete.
items.cn: finishen 意为完成。

items.en: Finish named the end of a race.
items.cn: finish 指比赛的终点。

items.en: Finish also named a surface treatment.
items.cn: finish 又指表面处理。

note.en: Finish is compared with similar-looking words and with words for completing.
note.cn: 把 finish 与形近词以及表示完成的词作比较。

entries.definition: to bring something to a close

normalIntro.en: Finish moves from doing the last step to naming the last point.
normalIntro.cn: finish 从做最后一步，延伸到命名最后那个点。

normal.en: Finish your homework before dinner.
The film finishes at nine.
The finish line is close.
A smooth finish makes wood shine.
normal.cn: 光滑的表面处理让木头发亮。

normal.en: Add a finishing touch to the cake.
normal.cn: 给蛋糕加上最后的点缀。

abstract.en: Every ending is also a boundary drawn in time.
abstract.cn: 每一个结束，也是在时间里画下的一道边界。

abstract.en: To finish is to decide that enough has been done.
abstract.cn: 完成，就是决定已经做得足够。

abstract.en: The last touch often reveals the whole craft.
abstract.cn: 最后一步，往往显露整门手艺。

examples.en: She finished the last question and put down her pen.
examples.cn: 她答完最后一题，放下了笔。

examples.en: The meeting finished at noon.
examples.cn: 会议在中午结束。

examples.en: The table has a smooth finish.
examples.cn: 这张桌子表面很光滑。

dict_mnemonic.text: finish 源自拉丁语 finis（结束），经古法语 finir 进入英语，核心义「做到尽头」。

root: 源自拉丁语 finis（结束、界限），核心义「到达尽头」。

sensesIntro.en: Finish means to complete, to end, the end point, or a surface treatment.
sensesIntro.cn: finish 意为完成、结束、终点或表面处理。

core.en: Reaching the end of a task or object.
core.cn: 到达任务或物体的尽头。

branches.en: Doing the last step of a task.
The final treatment of a surface.
The action and the place share one word.
branches.cn: 动作与位置共用一个词。

intro.en: Finish grows from the Latin root finis through French and English suffixes.
intro.cn: finish 从拉丁词根 finis 出发，经由法语和英语后缀生长。

latinIntro.en: The Latin finis and finire also gave final, finance, and define.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 finis 与 finire 也孕育了 final、finance 和 define。

items.example: I will finish the report tonight.
An unfinished painting stood on the easel.
items.exampleCN: 画架上放着一幅未完成的画。
他们给旧地板重新做了表面处理。

definition_en: flames that burn, a destructive burning, a stove or fireplace, the shooting of guns, or to dismiss someone from a job
core_image: 黑夜里的火堆噼啪作响，橘红的火舌向上卷
scene: 孩子们围坐在火堆旁取暖。The children sat around the fire to keep warm.
sceneCN: 这里 fire 是「火」（第 1 个义项）；句意：孩子们围坐在火堆旁取暖。

senses.title: Burning flames
senses.definition: the heat and light produced by burning
senses.definitionCN: 燃烧产生的热与光
senses.example: The children sat around the fire to keep warm.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们围坐在火堆旁取暖。
senses.why: This is the oldest and most basic sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老、最基本的义项。

senses.title: Destructive burning
senses.definition: a burning that destroys buildings or land
senses.definitionCN: 烧毁建筑或土地的燃烧
senses.example: A fire broke out in the warehouse.
senses.exampleCN: 仓库里发生了一场火灾。
senses.why: The same element can become a disaster.
senses.whyCN: 同一种元素也可能变成灾难。

senses.title: Hearth fire
senses.definition: a fireplace or stove used for heat or cooking
senses.definitionCN: 用于取暖或烹饪的壁炉或炉子
senses.example: They gathered by the fire in the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 他们聚在厨房的炉火旁。
senses.why: A controlled fire warms the home.
senses.whyCN: 被控制的火温暖着家。

senses.title: Shooting
senses.definition: the act of shooting a gun
senses.definitionCN: 开枪射击的行为
senses.example: The soldiers opened fire at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵们在黎明时开火。
senses.why: Guns produce a flash like fire.
senses.whyCN: 枪口喷出的火光如同火焰。

senses.title: To dismiss
senses.definition: to make someone leave their job
senses.definitionCN: 让某人离开工作岗位
senses.example: The manager fired him for being late.
senses.exampleCN: 经理因他迟到而解雇了他。
senses.why: The verb image is throwing someone out.
senses.whyCN: 动词的画面感是「把人赶出去」。

intro.en: Fire is one of the oldest English words, from Proto-Germanic fōr and Old English fyr.
intro.cn: fire 是英语中最古老的词之一，来自原始日耳曼语 fōr 和古英语 fyr。

items.en: For named the heat of burning.

items.en: Fyr meant fire and burning.

items.en: Fire kept the same core meaning.

items.en: Fire named the shooting of guns.

items.en: The verb came to mean to dismiss.

note.en: Fire is compared with similar-looking words and with words for flame and dismissal.

entries.definition: the bright gas of a fire

normalIntro.en: Fire is heat that warms, burns, shoots, and even ends a job.

normal.en: We sat by the fire and told stories.
The forest fire spread quickly.
The fire alarm woke everyone.
normal.cn: 火警警报叫醒了所有人。

normal.en: The soldiers opened fire.
The boss fired two workers.

abstract.cn: 火是既能温暖家园、也能毁掉它的能量。

abstract.en: A spark contains both danger and possibility.
abstract.cn: 一点火星既含危险，也含可能。

definition_en: a person whose job is to put out fires, or a person who tends a fire in a furnace or engine
core_image: 浓烟里，一个戴头盔的身影抱着水带向前冲

senses.title: Firefighter
senses.definition: a person whose job is to put out dangerous fires
senses.definitionCN: 以扑灭危险火灾为职业的人
senses.example: The fireman rushed into the smoke to save people.
senses.exampleCN: 消防员冲进浓烟里去救人。

senses.title: Stoker

normal.en: Firemen train to move through smoke.

senses.why: Suitability is the broadest sense.
senses.whyCN: 适合性是最宽泛的义项。

senses.title: Healthy
senses.definition: healthy and strong, especially through exercise
senses.definitionCN: 健康强壮的，尤指通过锻炼
senses.example: She runs to keep fit.
senses.exampleCN: 她跑步以保持健康。
senses.why: A body in good shape is fit.
senses.whyCN: 状态良好的身体就是 fit。

senses.title: Right size
senses.definition: to be the right size or shape for someone
senses.definitionCN: 尺寸或形状正好适合某人
senses.example: This pair of shoes fits well.
senses.exampleCN: 这双鞋很合脚。
senses.why: Clothing is the everyday testing ground.
senses.whyCN: 衣服是这个词最常见的测试场。

senses.title: To suit
senses.definition: to be suitable for something or someone
senses.definitionCN: 适合某事或某人
senses.example: The job fits her skills.
senses.exampleCN: 这份工作适合她的技能。
senses.why: What matches a need fits it.
senses.whyCN: 与需求相匹配，就是适合。

senses.title: To install
senses.definition: to put a part or device into place
senses.definitionCN: 把部件或装置放到正确位置
senses.example: They fitted a new lock.
senses.exampleCN: 他们装了一把新锁。
senses.why: A part that fits is placed in place.
senses.whyCN: 能贴合的部分被安置到位。

intro.en: Fit appeared in late Middle English with the sense of matching or being suited; its deeper origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: fit 出现在中古英语晚期，意为「相配、适合」，更早的来源并不确定。

items.en: Fit meant a match or a contest.
items.cn: fit 指匹配或较量。

items.en: Fit came to mean suited or proper.
items.cn: fit 引申为适合的、恰当的。

items.en: Fit described clothing that matches the body.
items.cn: fit 描述衣服与身体相合。

items.en: Fit meant healthy and in good condition.
items.cn: fit 意为健康、状态良好。

items.en: The verb named the placing of a part.
items.cn: 动词形式指把部件安装到位。

note.en: Fit is compared with similar-looking words and with words for suitability and health.
note.cn: 把 fit 与形近词以及表示适合和健康的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Fit links a good match: clothes that match the body, work that matches skills, a part that matches its place.
normalIntro.cn: fit 连接着各种「相配」：衣服配身体、工作配技能、零件配位置。

normal.en: These shoes fit perfectly.
Exercise keeps you fit.
The key fits the lock.
He fits in well at school.
They fitted new windows.

abstract.en: To fit is to find the place where something belongs.
abstract.cn: 适合，就是找到某物所属的位置。

abstract.en: A healthy body and a proper word share the same name.
abstract.cn: 健康的身体与恰当的词，共用一个名字。

abstract.en: What fits does not need force.
abstract.cn: 真正合适的东西，不需要硬塞。

examples.en: This pair of shoes fits well.
examples.cn: 这双鞋很合脚。

examples.en: She runs to keep fit.
examples.cn: 她跑步以保持健康。

examples.en: They fitted a new lock.
examples.cn: 他们装了一把新锁。

dict_mnemonic.text: fit 是中古英语晚期出现的词，核心义「相配、合适」，后引申出健康与安装。

root: 源自中古英语 fit（相配、较量），更深来源不确定，核心义「恰好相合」。

sensesIntro.en: Fit means suitable, healthy, right in size, suited to something, or to install.
sensesIntro.cn: fit 意为合适的、健康的、合身、适合或安装。

core.en: A match between a thing and its purpose or place.
core.cn: 事物与其用途或位置之间的契合。

branches.en: A match of skills and tasks.
A part placed where it belongs.
branches.cn: 零件被安放到应在的位置。

intro.en: Fit is a short Middle English word that forms many everyday compounds.
intro.cn: fit 是中古英语的短词，构成了许多日常复合词。

latinIntro.en: Fit has no Latin ancestor; Latin aptus, fitted, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: fit 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 aptus（合适的）只是语义对应词。

items.example: It was a fitting end to the day.
items.exampleCN: 这是这一天恰如其分的结尾。

items.example: The water is unfit to drink.

items.exampleCN: 她穿了一身亮眼的衣服。

definition_en: the number 5, a group of five things, or the age of five
core_image: 一只手张开，五根手指在灯下清清楚楚
scene: 桌上有五个苹果。There are five apples on the table.
sceneCN: 这里 five 是「五」（第 1 个义项）；句意：桌上有五个苹果。

senses.title: The number five
senses.definition: the number equal to four plus one
senses.definitionCN: 等于四加一的数字
senses.example: There are five apples on the table.
senses.exampleCN: 桌上有五个苹果。
senses.why: This is the basic counting sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的计数义项。

senses.title: A group of five
senses.definition: a set or group of five things or people
senses.definitionCN: 由五个事物或人组成的一组
senses.example: The players lined up in fives.
senses.exampleCN: 队员们五人一组排好队。
senses.why: Numbers also name groups.
senses.whyCN: 数字也能命名成组的单位。

senses.title: Age five
senses.definition: the age of five years
senses.definitionCN: 五岁的年龄
senses.example: She started school at five.
senses.exampleCN: 她五岁开始上学。
senses.why: A number can mark a stage of life.
senses.whyCN: 数字也能标记人生的阶段。

intro.en: Five goes back to Proto-Germanic fimf and further to an ancient Indo-European root for five.
intro.cn: five 上溯至原始日耳曼语 fimf，更早则来自表示「五」的古老印欧词根。

items.en: Penkwe meant five.
items.cn: penkwe 意为五。

items.en: Fimf meant five.
items.cn: fimf 意为五。

items.en: Fif meant five.
items.cn: fif 意为五。

items.en: Five took its modern form.
items.cn: five 形成现代拼写。

items.en: Five also named groups and ages.
items.cn: five 也用来指成组数量与年龄。

note.en: Five is compared with similar-looking words and with other number words.
note.cn: 把 five 与形近词以及其他数词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Five fits neatly on one open hand, and it counts things, groups, and years.
normalIntro.cn: five 恰好落在一只张开的手上，用来数东西、数成组的人、也数年岁。

normal.en: A hand has five fingers.
We waited five minutes.
The meeting starts at five.
She has a five-star rating.
The fifth day was the coldest.

abstract.en: Five is the number of the open hand.
abstract.cn: 五，是张开的手掌之数。

abstract.en: Small numbers let us take the measure of the world.
abstract.cn: 小小的数字，让我们丈量世界。

abstract.en: Counting is one of the oldest human habits.
abstract.cn: 计数是人类最古老的习惯之一。

examples.en: There are five apples on the table.
examples.cn: 桌上有五个苹果。

examples.en: She started school at five.
examples.cn: 她五岁开始上学。

examples.en: The players lined up in fives.
examples.cn: 队员们五人一组排好队。

dict_mnemonic.text: five 来自古英语 fif，与德语 fünf 同源，核心义就是数字「五」。

root: 源自古英语 fif（五），与德语 fünf、拉丁语 quinque 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Five means the number 5, a group of five, or the age of five.
sensesIntro.cn: five 意为数字五、五个一组或五岁。

core.en: The count of one hand's fingers.
core.cn: 一只手的指数。

branches.cn: 由五个事物组成的一组。

branches.en: Number and group share one form.
branches.cn: 数字与成组共用一个形式。

intro.en: Five is a native Germanic number word that builds a whole family of numbers.
intro.cn: five 是日耳曼语本族数词，能构成一整族数字词。

latinIntro.en: Five has no Latin ancestor; Latin quinque, five, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: five 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 quinque（五）只是语义对应词。

items.example: Five birds sat on the wire.

items.exampleCN: 他用一张五元钞票付款。
